speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these symptoms like fatigue, abdominal pain, and night sweats? Also, have you noticed any fever or unexplained itching?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has this abdominal pain been constant, or does it come and go, and have you noticed any lumps or swelling in other areas like your neck or armpits?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your fixed, painless neck swelling and systemic symptoms, have you experienced any persistent cough or shortness of breath? Also, have you had any recent travel or exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fullness in your abdomen suggests possible liver or spleen enlargement, so I need to check for other signs like pale skin or easy bruising. Have you noticed any dark urine, light-colored stools, or unusual bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your smoking history and the combination of abdominal fullness, weight loss, and a fixed supraclavicular node, I am concerned for an underlying malignancy. I would like to proceed with imaging to evaluate the extent of the disease. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis. REQUEST TEST: Chest_CTA.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Scan_Thorax_and_Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Complete_Blood_Count: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal. Lactate_Dehydrogenase: Elevated. Cervical_Lymph_Node_Biopsy: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Vital_Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood_Pressure 135/80 mmHg, Heart_Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory_Rate 14 breaths/min. Neck_Examination: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node observed. Abdominal_Examination: Slight abdominal distension, Normal bowel sounds, Dullness over left lower quadrant, Splenomegaly detected without rebound tenderness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index, combined with your B-symptoms and widespread lymphadenopathy, strongly point to a specific type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. I believe we have enough information to finalize the assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL).
